findings.requirement: Parents may visit the center during hours of operation without prior approval to observe their child and program.
findings.quote: Ensuring parents can visit the child-care center any time during the child-care center's hours of operation to observe their child, program activities, the building, the grounds, and the equipment without having to secure prior approval
findings.handbook_quote: Parents are welcome to visit at any time during our hours, without calling first.
findings.explanation: The handbook tells parents they may visit at any time during operating hours without calling first.

findings.requirement: If the center does not carry required liability insurance, parents must be notified in writing before admission.
findings.quote: If you do not carry liability insurance that meets the requirements of §746.203 of this division (relating to What are the liability insurance requirements?), then you must notify the parent of each child in your care in writing that you do not carry liability insurance before you admit the child into your care.
findings.handbook_quote: Little Acorns carries general liability insurance at each of our centers.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that the center carries liability insurance, so the no-insurance notice is not needed.

findings.requirement: The center must have written operational policies and procedures covering at least the minimum topics listed in the rule.
findings.quote: You must develop written operational policies and procedures that at a minimum address each of the following
findings.handbook_quote: This handbook explains how our centers work and what you can expect from us.
findings.explanation: The handbook covers many operational topics but does not address every required topic, such as suspension and expulsion, immunization requirements, emergency preparedness, breastfeeding support, vaccine-preventable disease policy, and inclusive services.
findings.fix: Our written operational policies address all required topics, including hours and release procedures, illness and medication, emergencies and parent notifications, discipline, safe sleep, meals, screenings, enrollment, transportation, water activities, field trips, animals, physical activity, insect repellent and sunscreen, parent rights, questions and concerns, emergency preparedness, breastfeeding support, suspension and expulsion, immunization requirements, vaccine-preventable disease policy, and inclusive services for children with special care needs.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the center's hours, days, and months of operation and its procedures for releasing children.
findings.quote: (1) Hours, days, and months of operation [Medium]; (2) Procedures for the release of children [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: Our centers are open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., all year except for the following holidays
findings.explanation: The handbook states operating hours and explains that children are released only to parents or authorized adults.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state illness and exclusion criteria and medication procedures or that medication is not dispensed.
findings.quote: (3) Illness and exclusion criteria [Medium]; (4) Procedures for dispensing medication or a statement that medication is not dispensed [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: please keep your child home if they have a fever of 100.4°F or higher, vomiting, diarrhea, an unexplained rash, or are too sick to take part in normal activities.
findings.explanation: The handbook states illness exclusion criteria and explains that prescription and over-the-counter medicine can be given.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state procedures for handling medical emergencies and for parental notifications.
findings.quote: (5) Procedures for handling medical emergencies [Medium]; (6) Procedures for parental notifications [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: For a serious injury we will call 911 first and then call you right away.
findings.explanation: The handbook explains emergency response and how parents are notified about illness and injury.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include discipline and guidance consistent with Subchapter L.
findings.quote: Punishment associated with food, naps, or toilet training [High]
findings.handbook_quote: Children who throw food or refuse to sit at lunch may lose their dessert for that day.
findings.explanation: Taking away dessert as a consequence is punishment associated with food.
findings.fix: We never use food as a reward or punishment. If a child throws food or refuses to sit at lunch, a teacher will use positive guidance such as redirection and a brief time-out, not take away food.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include a safe sleep policy for infants from birth through 12 months old.
findings.quote: If an infant falls asleep in a restrictive device, you must remove the infant from the device and place the infant in a crib as soon as possible [High]
findings.handbook_quote: To avoid waking a baby, infants who fall asleep in a bouncer, swing or car seat may finish their nap there as long as a teacher can see them.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows an infant to finish a nap in a bouncer, swing, or car seat, but the rule requires moving the infant to a crib as soon as possible.
findings.fix: If an infant falls asleep in a bouncer, swing, car seat, or other restrictive device, a teacher will move the infant to their own crib as soon as possible. Infants sleep only in their own cribs, on their backs, with no blankets, pillows, or toys.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state hearing and vision screening requirements and enrollment procedures, including how and when parents are notified of policy changes.
findings.quote: (12) Hearing and vision screening requirements [Medium]; (13) Enrollment procedures, including how and when parents will be notified of policy changes
findings.handbook_quote: To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes enrollment steps but does not explain how or when parents are notified of policy changes.
findings.fix: Enrollment procedures. Families complete our registration form, enrollment agreement, emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and health and immunization records. We will notify families in writing of any policy change before it takes effect, and at least [number] days in advance when possible.

findings.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state transportation and water activity procedures.
findings.quote: (14) Transportation, if applicable [Medium]; (15) Water activities, if applicable [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: We don't offer swimming or wading pools. Children may play at a water table with a teacher present.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that the center does not offer swimming or wading pools and describes water table play and transportation permission.

findings.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state field trip and animal procedures.
findings.quote: Notify parents in writing when animals are or will be present [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: We don't keep classroom pets; if a visitor brings an animal, we tell families in advance.
findings.explanation: The handbook says families are told in advance, but the rule requires written notice when animals are or will be present.
findings.fix: If a visitor brings an animal to the center or on a field trip, we will notify families in writing in advance.

findings.requirement: The handbook must promote indoor and outdoor physical activity consistent with Subchapter F.
findings.quote: Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity that is consistent with Subchapter F of this chapter
findings.handbook_quote: Physical activity. Active play helps children grow strong, sleep well and learn. Every day, children have time for running, climbing, dancing and ball games, both outdoors on our playground and indoors in our movement room when the weather keeps us in.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes benefits, types, and settings for active play but does not state the duration of physical activity, recommended clothing and footwear, weather criteria, or the plan for activity during extreme weather.
findings.fix: Physical activity. Active play helps children grow strong, sleep well, and learn. Children have at least [number] minutes of moderate to vigorous active play each day, both outdoors on our playground and indoors in our movement room when weather keeps us inside. Teachers lead at least two short active games each day and join in the play. Children should wear [clothing and footwear] that allows free and safe movement. We cancel or shorten outdoor play only when extreme weather poses a significant health risk, and on those days we increase indoor physical activity so children still get their full activity time.

findings.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state procedures for providing and applying insect repellant and sunscreen.
findings.quote: Procedures for providing and applying, as needed, insect repellant and sunscreen, including what types will be used, if applicable [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: With your written permission, we apply the sunscreen you provide before outdoor play, and insect repellent when needed.
findings.explanation: The handbook explains written permission, who provides products, labeling, and when products are applied.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state parent rights consistent with Division 5 of Subchapter B.
findings.quote: Parent rights that are consistent with the rules in Division 5 of this subchapter (relating to Parent Rights) [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: Your rights as a parent. You have the right to visit your child at any time we are open, to see your child's records, to see our most recent licensing inspection report (posted at the entrance), and to contact the state licensing agency with any concern about our program.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists some parent rights but omits several rights in Division 5, such as accessing compliance history and reviewing staff training records.
findings.fix: Your rights as a parent include visiting at any time we are open; filing a complaint; reviewing our publicly accessible records and your child's records; receiving our inspection reports and information about how to view our compliance history online; having us follow a valid court order about pickup; receiving Child Care Regulation contact information; viewing available video of an alleged incident involving your child with the required notices; receiving our policies; reviewing staff training records and in-house training curriculum on request; and being free from retaliation for using these rights.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state procedures for parents to review and discuss questions or concerns with the director.
findings.quote: Procedures for parents to review and discuss with the child-care center director any questions or concerns about the policies and procedures of the child-care center [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: Please talk with your child's teacher first; if your concern isn't resolved, ask for a meeting with the center director, who will meet with you within three business days.
findings.explanation: The handbook explains how parents can raise questions or concerns and meet with the director.

findings.requirement: Children's records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation for emergency use.
findings.quote: All children’s records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation for use in an emergency.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention that children's records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation.

findings.requirement: Employees must report suspected abuse, neglect, and exploitation to DFPS as required by law.
findings.quote: Reporting and ensuring your employees and volunteers report suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation directly to the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline, as required by Texas Family Code §261.10; an employee may not delegate the responsibility to make a report, and you may not require an employee to seek approval to file a report or notify you that a report was made
findings.handbook_quote: If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director, who looks into the concern and decides whether to contact child protective services.
findings.explanation: The handbook routes suspected abuse or neglect through the director for a decision, but employees must report directly and may not seek approval.
findings.fix: If any staff member suspects a child has been abused, neglected, or exploited, the staff member reports it directly to the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline at 1-800-252-5400. Staff do not need to tell the director first or get permission before making a report, and the director will also be notified after the report is made.

findings.requirement: Classroom ratios are based on the specified age of the children in the group and must not be exceeded.
findings.quote: The classroom ratio is the number of children one caregiver may supervise and is shown in the following chart.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists one caregiver for 20 four-year-olds, but the rule allows one caregiver to supervise at most 18 four-year-olds.
findings.note: Beam flagged this as a conflict, but the words it quoted don't appear in your handbook exactly as written (it may have joined two lines, such as two rows of a table).

findings.requirement: Infants must be placed face-up for sleep in their own crib unless a health-care professional documents a different position is medically necessary.
findings.quote: You must place an infant in a face-up sleeping position in the infant's own crib, unless you have a completed Sleep Exception Form that includes a signed statement from a health-care professional stating that a different sleeping position for the child is medically necessary
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that infants are placed on their backs to sleep in cribs without blankets, pillows, or toys.

findings.requirement: There must be no harsh, cruel, or unusual treatment of any child, including prohibited discipline practices.
findings.quote: Punishment associated with food, naps, or toilet training [High]
findings.handbook_quote: Children who throw food or refuse to sit at lunch may lose their dessert for that day.
findings.explanation: Taking away dessert as a consequence is punishment associated with food.
findings.fix: We never use food as a reward or punishment. If a child throws food or refuses to sit at lunch, a teacher will use positive guidance such as redirection and a brief time-out, not take away food.

findings.requirement: Parents must be notified at least 48 hours in advance of a field trip with destination and expected return time.
findings.quote: You must notify the parent of each child who will be on the field trip, indicating when and where the child will be going, and when the child is expected to return to the child-care center. The notice must be posted at least 48 hours in advance of a field trip.
findings.handbook_quote: We'll let you know about walking trips on the morning of the trip.
findings.explanation: Walking trips are announced the morning of the trip, which is less than the required 48 hours' notice.
findings.fix: We will post notice of every field trip, including walking trips, at least 48 hours in advance in a prominent place. The notice will say where and when children are going and when they are expected to return.

findings.requirement: Meals and snacks must follow USDA CACFP meal patterns regardless of reimbursement participation.
findings.quote: The meals and snacks must follow the meal patterns established by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook says meals meet USDA nutrition guidelines but does not state they follow the CACFP meal patterns required by the rule.
findings.fix: Our meals and snacks follow the meal patterns established by the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), whether or not we receive reimbursement.

findings.requirement: Unless licensed for get-well care, an ill child must not attend if the listed illness conditions exist.
findings.quote: Unless you are licensed to provide get-well care, you must not allow an ill child to attend your child-care center if one or more of the following exists:
findings.handbook_quote: please keep your child home if they have a fever of 100.4°F or higher, vomiting, diarrhea, an unexplained rash, or are too sick to take part in normal activities.
findings.explanation: The handbook states illness conditions that require a child to stay home.

findings.requirement: Medication may be administered only with parent authorization obtained in writing, electronically, or by telephone for a single dose.
findings.quote: Authorization to administer medication to a child in your care must be obtained from the child’s parent: (1) In writing, signed and dated [Medium-High]; (2) In an electronic format that is capable of being viewed and saved [Medium-High]; or (3) By telephone to administer a single dose of a medication. [Medium-High]
findings.handbook_quote: you may authorize medication by phone or by text message to your child's teacher, and we will note your permission in the medication log.
findings.explanation: Phone authorization is allowed only for a single dose, and text messages are not listed as an authorization method unless saved as an electronic record.
findings.fix: You may authorize medication in writing, through an electronic form we can view and save, or by phone for one dose only. We will record every authorization and dose in the medication log.

findings.requirement: A food allergy emergency plan is required for each child with a health-care-professional-diagnosed food allergy.
findings.quote: You must have a food allergy emergency plan for each child with a known food allergy that has been diagnosed by a health-care professional.
findings.handbook_quote: Please tell us in writing about any food allergy. For children with a severe allergy, we need an allergy action plan signed by the child's health care provider before the child's first day.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires an allergy action plan only for severe allergies, but the rule requires a plan for every health-care-professional-diagnosed food allergy.
findings.fix: If a health care professional has diagnosed your child with any food allergy, please give us a food allergy emergency plan signed and dated by the health care professional and parent before the child's first day. We will keep it in your child's file.

findings.requirement: A child may be released only to a parent or a person designated by the parent.
findings.quote: You must release a child only to a parent or a person designated by the parent.
findings.handbook_quote: We release children only to parents and to adults listed on the child's authorized pickup form.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that children are released only to parents or adults on the authorized pickup form.

findings.requirement: The center must practice a fire drill every month and children must be able to exit safely within three minutes.
findings.quote: You must practice a fire drill every month. The children must be able to safely exit the building within three minutes
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly.
findings.explanation: The handbook says fire drills are practiced monthly but does not state that children must be able to exit safely within three minutes.
findings.fix: We practice a fire drill every month. Our goal is for all children and staff to leave the building safely within three minutes.

findings.requirement: Return after illness based only on being fever-free
findings.quote: A child who was ill may return to your child-care center when: (1) The child is free of symptoms of illness for 24 hours [Medium]; or (2) You have obtained a health care professional's statement that the child no longer has an excludable disease or condition. [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: Children may return when they have been fever-free for 24 hours without medicine.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows return after being fever-free, but the rule requires being free of symptoms of illness for 24 hours or a health care professional's statement.
findings.fix: A child may return after being free of symptoms of illness for 24 hours, or sooner with a health care professional's written statement that the child is no longer contagious or has no excludable condition.

TX.summary: The handbook covers many required policies but conflicts with the rules on safe sleep, discipline, abuse reporting, ratios, field-trip notice, medication authorization, and animal notice. Several items are only partially addressed, including enrollment notice, physical activity, parent rights, CACFP meal patterns, food allergy plans, and fire-drill timing.

NC.rulebook: Chapter 9 Child Care Rules, effective July 1, 2025 (DCDEE)

findings.requirement: Parents must be allowed access during operating hours to contact the child or evaluate caregiving space and care, after notifying the on-site administrator.
findings.quote: The parent of a child enrolled in a child care center shall be allowed access to the center during its operating hours for the purposes of contacting the child or evaluating caregiving space at the center and the care provided by the center for the child. The parent shall notify the on-site administrator of his or her presence upon entering the premises.
findings.handbook_quote: Parents are welcome to visit at any time during our hours, without calling first.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows visits but does not tell parents to notify the on-site administrator when they arrive.
findings.fix: Parents are welcome to visit during our operating hours. Please check in with the on-site administrator when you arrive so we can help you connect with your child and answer questions.

findings.requirement: Parents subject to custody court orders may access the center only in accordance with the court order.
findings.quote: Parents subject to court orders related to custody of a child enrolled in a child care center shall only be allowed access to the center in accordance with the court order.
findings.handbook_quote: Parents are welcome to visit at any time during our hours, without calling first.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention access for parents subject to custody court orders.

findings.requirement: The operator must not knowingly permit a person convicted of a reportable conviction on the premises.
findings.quote: The child care operator shall not knowingly permit a person on the premises of a child care center who has been convicted of a "reportable conviction" as defined in G.S. 14-208.6(4).
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that persons with reportable convictions are not permitted on the premises.

findings.requirement: Each child must have an immunization record on file, and children's records must be available for Division review.
findings.quote: children's records that include an application for enrollment, medical and immunization records, and permission to seek emergency medical care;
findings.handbook_quote: To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires an immunization record as part of enrollment.

findings.requirement: All required records must be available at the center during operating hours for Division review.
findings.quote: Each center shall maintain records as described in 10A NCAC 09 .0302(d) and shall make them available to the Division for review.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child's records are confidential and are shared only with you, our staff and licensing staff.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that records are shared with licensing staff.

findings.requirement: Children must have minimum daily outdoor time when weather conditions permit, based on program hours and ages.
findings.quote: When children are in care and weather conditions permit, there shall be outdoor time, either as part of a small group, a whole group, or individual activity, for no less than the following durations:
findings.handbook_quote: Children play outside at least twice a day unless the weather is dangerous.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state the minimum daily outdoor time required by age and program hours.
findings.fix: Children play outside every day when weather conditions permit. We provide at least 30 minutes of outdoor time for children under 2, at least 30 minutes for children in programs under 5 hours, and at least 60 minutes for children 2 and older in programs of 5 hours or more.

findings.requirement: Screen time for preschool children three and older must stimulate a developmental domain, be limited to 30 minutes per day and 2.5 hours per week, and be documented.
findings.quote: when screen time is provided on any electronic media device with a visual display, it shall be: (A) offered to stimulate a developmental domain in accordance with the North Carolina Foundations for Early Learning and Development as referenced in Rule .0508 of this Section; (B) limited to 30 minutes per day and no more than a total of two and a half hours per week, per child; and (C) documented on a cumulative log or the activity plan
findings.handbook_quote: Screen time is limited to occasional educational programs.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state the developmental purpose, time limits, or documentation required for preschool screen time.
findings.fix: For children 3 and older, screen time is used only to support a developmental domain, is limited to 30 minutes per day and 2.5 hours per week per child, and is documented on our activity plan or screen-time log.

findings.requirement: Each group must have at least four of the five activity areas available daily, with the fifth available at least monthly.
findings.quote: For each group of children in care, the center shall provide daily four of the five activity areas listed in G.S. 110-91(12) as follows:
findings.handbook_quote: Each day includes indoor and outdoor play, circle time, small-group activities, meals and rest.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention the required activity areas.

findings.requirement: Screen time is prohibited for children under three years of age.
findings.quote: Screen time, including television, videos, video games, and computer usage, shall be prohibited for children under three years of age.
findings.handbook_quote: Screen time is limited to occasional educational programs.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows screen time for all ages, while the rule prohibits screen time for children under three.
findings.fix: We do not use screen time for children under three. For children three and older, screen time is limited to 30 minutes per day and 2.5 hours per week, supports a developmental domain, and is documented.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the days and hours the center operates.
findings.quote: The operational policies shall include at least the following information: (1) the days and hours the center operates;
findings.handbook_quote: Our centers are open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., all year except for the following holidays
findings.explanation: The handbook states the days and hours of operation.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the age range of children served.
findings.quote: (2) the age range of the children served;
findings.handbook_quote: We are a nonprofit early learning program serving children from 6 weeks through 5 years old, with after-school care for children up to age 12 at our Austin location.
findings.explanation: The handbook states the ages of children served.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe admission requirements and enrollment procedures.
findings.quote: (3) admission requirements and enrollment procedures;
findings.handbook_quote: To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes enrollment forms and completion requirements.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state parent fees and the payment plan.
findings.quote: (4) parent fees and payment plan;
findings.handbook_quote: Tuition is billed monthly and is due on the 1st of each month through autopay. A late fee of $25 applies to payments received after the 5th.
findings.explanation: The handbook states tuition, due dates, late fees, and payment information.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe services provided, such as meals, before and after school care, and transportation.
findings.quote: (5) information about services provided by the center, such as number of meals served, before and after school care, and transportation;
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes meals and other services such as after-school care and field trips.

findings.requirement: The handbook must list any items parents must provide.
findings.quote: (6) items, if any, to be provided by parents;
findings.handbook_quote: With your written permission, we apply the sunscreen you provide before outdoor play, and insect repellent when needed.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists items parents provide, such as sunscreen and insect repellent.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include a schedule of daily, weekly, and monthly cleaning duties.
findings.quote: (7) a schedule of daily, weekly, and monthly cleaning duties;
findings.handbook_quote: We take children's safety very seriously. If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director
findings.explanation: The handbook does not include a schedule of daily, weekly, and monthly cleaning duties.
findings.fix: Our cleaning schedule includes daily, weekly, and monthly tasks for classrooms, restrooms, kitchens, and outdoor areas. A copy is available from the director.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include written procedures for reporting suspected child abuse and neglect.
findings.quote: (8) written procedures for reporting suspected child abuse and neglect;
findings.handbook_quote: If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director, who looks into the concern and decides whether to contact child protective services.
findings.explanation: The handbook includes written procedures for reporting suspected abuse and neglect.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the center's discipline policy for behavior management.
findings.quote: (9) the center's discipline policy for behavior management;
findings.handbook_quote: We use positive guidance: clear expectations, redirection, praise and natural consequences. We never use spanking, shaking or any physical punishment, and we never shame or yell at children.
findings.explanation: The handbook states the center's discipline policy.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe opportunities for parent participation.
findings.quote: (10) a description of opportunities for parent participation; and
findings.handbook_quote: We share updates through our parent app and hold parent-teacher conferences twice a year.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes opportunities for parent participation.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include nutrition policies.
findings.quote: (10) a description of opportunities for parent participation; and (11) nutrition policies.
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines. The daily menu, including all meals and snacks, is posted at the entrance of each center.
findings.explanation: The handbook includes nutrition policies.

findings.requirement: Operational policies must be discussed with parents on or before the child's first day and a copy given to parents.
findings.quote: Operational policies shall be discussed with parents on or before the child's first day of attendance in the center. A copy of the policies shall be given to the parents on or before the child's first day of attendance and the parents shall be notified in writing of all changes in policy.
findings.handbook_quote: I have received and read the Little Acorns Family Handbook and agree to follow its policies.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that operational policies are discussed and given to parents on or before the first day.
findings.fix: We give you a copy of this handbook and review it with you on or before your child's first day. We also notify you in writing of any policy changes.

findings.requirement: Parents must be notified in writing of all policy changes.
findings.quote: the parents shall be notified in writing of all changes in policy.
findings.handbook_quote: I have received and read the Little Acorns Family Handbook and agree to follow its policies.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that parents are notified in writing of policy changes.
findings.fix: We notify families in writing of any changes to our policies.

findings.requirement: Copies of operational policies and changes must be distributed to staff.
findings.quote: Copies of operational policies and any subsequent changes to those policies shall be distributed to the staff.
findings.handbook_quote: I have received and read the Little Acorns Family Handbook and agree to follow its policies.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that operational policies and changes are distributed to staff.
findings.fix: We give staff copies of our operational policies and any changes.

findings.requirement: The center must have a plan encouraging parent participation and informing parents about the program and services.
findings.quote: Each center shall have a plan that will encourage parent participation and inform parents about the program and its services. The plan shall be discussed with parents on or before the child's first day of attendance and shall be posted in the center or a copy shall be given to parents on or before the child's first day of attendance.
findings.handbook_quote: We share updates through our parent app and hold parent-teacher conferences twice a year.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe a parent participation plan that is reviewed and provided before the first day.
findings.fix: We have a plan to encourage parent participation and keep families informed about our program and services. We review this plan with you on or before your child's first day and provide a copy.

findings.requirement: The parent participation plan must include a procedure for parents who need information or have complaints about the program.
findings.quote: a procedure for parents who need information or have complaints about the child care program.
findings.handbook_quote: Please talk with your child's teacher first; if your concern isn't resolved, ask for a meeting with the center director, who will meet with you within three business days.
findings.explanation: The handbook includes a procedure for parents with questions or complaints.

findings.requirement: The center must provide a safe indoor and outdoor environment, with equipment in good repair and free of hazards.
findings.quote: All child care centers shall provide a safe indoor and outdoor environment for the children in care. (b) All equipment and furnishings shall be in good repair.
findings.handbook_quote: We take children's safety very seriously. If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe safe indoor and outdoor environments or equipment repair standards.

findings.requirement: The operator must notify parents in writing of the smoking and tobacco restriction.
findings.quote: The operator shall notify the parent of each child enrolled in the center, in writing, of the smoking and tobacco restriction.
findings.handbook_quote: We take children's safety very seriously. If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director
findings.explanation: The handbook does not notify parents in writing of a smoking and tobacco restriction.
findings.fix: Our centers are smoke-free and tobacco-free. We notify families in writing of this restriction.

findings.requirement: When non-ambulatory children are in care, a movable crib or other device must be available for evacuation and used during required drills.
findings.quote: When non-ambulatory children are in care, a crib or other device shall be available for evacuation in case of fire or other emergency. The crib or other device shall be fitted with wheels in order to be moveable, have a reinforced bottom, and shall be able to fit through the designated fire exit.
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention an evacuation crib or device for non-ambulatory children.

findings.requirement: Potentially hazardous items must be stored in locked areas, removed, or otherwise inaccessible to children.
findings.quote: In child care centers, potentially hazardous items, including power tools, nails, chemicals, propane stoves, lawn mowers, and gasoline or kerosene, whether or not intended for use by children, shall be stored in locked areas, removed from the premises, or otherwise inaccessible to children.
findings.handbook_quote: We don't keep classroom pets; if a visitor brings an animal, we tell families in advance.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention locked storage for hazardous items.

findings.requirement: Firearms and ammunition are prohibited in a licensed child care center unless carried by a law enforcement officer.
findings.quote: Firearms and ammunition are prohibited in a licensed child care center unless carried by a law enforcement officer.
findings.handbook_quote: We take children's safety very seriously. If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention firearms and ammunition restrictions.

findings.requirement: Fire drills must be practiced monthly and records maintained.
findings.quote: Fire drills shall be practiced monthly and records shall be maintained as required by 10A NCAC 09 .0302(d)(5).
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions monthly fire drills but not the required records.
findings.fix: We practice a fire drill every month and keep a record of each drill, including the date, time, evacuation time, and the staff member who led it.

findings.requirement: A shelter-in-place or lockdown drill must be conducted at least every three months, with records maintained.
findings.quote: A "shelter in place drill" or "lockdown drill" as defined in 10A NCAC 09 .0102 shall be conducted at least every three months and records shall be maintained as required by 10A NCAC 09 .0302(d)(8).
findings.handbook_quote: We also practice shelter-in-place and lockdown drills several times a year.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that these drills occur at least every three months or that records are kept.
findings.fix: We practice a shelter-in-place or lockdown drill at least every three months and keep a record of each drill.

findings.requirement: A first aid kit must be available on site and accessible to staff, and each staff member must know its location.
findings.quote: A First Aid kit shall be available on site and accessible to staff. Each staff member shall be aware of the location of the First Aid kit.
findings.handbook_quote: Every classroom has a first aid kit.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions first aid kits but not that staff know their location.
findings.fix: A first aid kit is available and accessible to staff in every classroom, and all staff know where it is kept.

findings.requirement: The outdoor play area must be protected by a fence at least four feet high.
findings.quote: The outdoor play area shall be protected by a fence. The height shall be a minimum of four feet and the top of the fence shall be free of protrusions.
findings.handbook_quote: Children play outside at least twice a day unless the weather is dangerous.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention outdoor play area fencing.

findings.requirement: Stationary outdoor equipment more than 18 inches high must be installed over protective surfacing with required depth and fall zones.
findings.quote: All stationary outdoor equipment more than 18 inches high shall be installed over protective surfacing. Footings which anchor equipment shall not be exposed.
findings.handbook_quote: Children play outside at least twice a day unless the weather is dangerous.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention protective surfacing for outdoor equipment.

findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook states back sleeping but does not mention written waivers.
findings.fix: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep unless we have a written waiver on file from a health care professional or parent, as allowed by state rules.

findings.requirement: No pillows, wedges, positioners, toys, blankets, bumper pads, quilts, sheepskins, loose bedding, towels, or washcloths may be placed with a sleeping infant 12 months or younger.
findings.quote: specifies no pillows, wedges or other positioners, pillow-like toys, blankets, toys, bumper pads, quilts, sheepskins, loose bedding, towels and washcloths, or other objects may be placed with a sleeping infant aged 12 months or younger;
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists some prohibited items but not the full list required for sleeping infants.
findings.fix: Babies sleep with no pillows, wedges, positioners, toys, blankets, bumper pads, quilts, sheepskins, loose bedding, towels, washcloths, or other objects in the crib.

findings.requirement: Children must not be swaddled.

findings.requirement: Infants 12 months or younger must sleep alone in a crib, bassinet, play pen, mat, or cot and not in sitting devices.

findings.handbook_quote: Infants sleep in individual cribs, following their own schedules.

findings.handbook_quote: We don't offer swimming or wading pools. Children may play at a water table with a teacher present.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention inflatable restrictions.

findings.requirement: One staff member must complete playground safety training and conduct monthly playground inspections.
findings.quote: Following completion of playground safety training as required by Rule .1102(e) of this Chapter, a monthly playground inspection shall be conducted by an individual trained in playground safety requirements.
findings.handbook_quote: Children play outside at least twice a day unless the weather is dangerous.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention playground safety training or monthly inspections.

findings.requirement: The center must post its written safe sleep policy in a prominent place in the infant room.
findings.quote: The center shall post a copy of its safe sleep policy about infant safe sleep practices in a prominent place in the infant room where parents and caregivers are able to view daily.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that the written safe sleep policy is posted in the infant room.

findings.requirement: The safe sleep policy must be given and explained to parents of infants on or before the first day of attendance, with a signed acknowledgement retained.
findings.quote: A copy of the center's safe sleep policy shall be given and explained to the parents of an infant aged 12 months or younger on or before the first day the infant attends the center. The parent shall sign a statement acknowledging the receipt and explanation of the policy.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that the safe sleep policy is given and explained to parents with a signed acknowledgment.
findings.fix: Before an infant's first day, we give and explain our safe sleep policy and ask you to sign an acknowledgment for your child's file.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive written notice of safe sleep policy amendments at least 14 days before implementation.
findings.quote: If a center amends its safe sleep policy, it shall give written notice of the amendment to the parents of all enrolled infants aged 12 months or younger at least 14 days before the amended policy is implemented.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that parents receive written notice of safe sleep policy amendments 14 days before implementation.
findings.fix: If we change our safe sleep policy, we give written notice at least 14 days before the change takes effect.

findings.requirement: Infants 12 months or younger are prohibited from sleeping in sitting devices, and infants who fall asleep in them must be moved to a crib, bassinet, play pen, mat, or cot.
findings.quote: specifies that infants aged 12 months or younger are prohibited from sleeping in sitting devices, including car safety seats, strollers, swings, and infant carriers. Infants that fall asleep in sitting devices shall be moved to a crib, bassinet, play pen, mat, or cot; and
findings.handbook_quote: To avoid waking a baby, infants who fall asleep in a bouncer, swing or car seat may finish their nap there as long as a teacher can see them.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows infants to finish naps in sitting devices, while the rule requires moving them to a crib, bassinet, play pen, mat, or cot.
findings.fix: If an infant falls asleep in a bouncer, swing, or car seat, we move the baby to a crib, bassinet, play pen, mat, or cot.

findings.requirement: The center must have a written Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan addressing natural and man-made disasters, developed after required training.
findings.quote: Upon completion of the Emergency Preparedness and Response in Child Care training, the trained staff shall develop the Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan. The Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan means a written plan that addresses how a child care center will respond to both natural and man-made disasters
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention a written Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan.

findings.requirement: All staff must review the Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan during orientation and annually, with documentation maintained.
findings.quote: All staff shall review the center's Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan during orientation and on an annual basis with the trained staff. Documentation of the review shall be maintained at the center in the individual's personnel file or in a file designated for emergency preparedness and response plan documents.
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention staff review of the emergency plan during orientation and annually.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive written notice of shaken baby policy changes 14 days before implementation.
findings.quote: If a child care center changes the policy at any time, the child care center shall give written notice of the change to the child's parent 14 days prior to the implementation of the new policy
findings.handbook_quote: We take children's safety very seriously. If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention written notice of shaken baby policy changes 14 days before implementation.
findings.fix: If we change our policy on preventing shaken baby syndrome and abusive head trauma, we give written notice 14 days before the change takes effect.

findings.requirement: Staff must meet health standards, including medical reports, TB testing or screening, and health questionnaires, with specified due dates.
findings.quote: Health and emergency information shall be obtained for staff members as specified in the chart below:
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention staff medical reports, tuberculosis testing or screening, or health questionnaires.

findings.requirement: The applicable staff-to-child ratio must be posted in each classroom where parents can view it at all times.
findings.quote: the staff/child ratio applicable to a classroom as described in this Paragraph shall be posted in that classroom in an area that parents are able to view at all times.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are grouped by age. We keep classes small so every child gets attention:
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention posting staff-to-child ratios in classrooms.

findings.requirement: A child care administrator must be on site for required weekly hours based on licensed capacity.
findings.quote: Each child care center shall have a child care administrator who shall be responsible for monitoring the program and overseeing administrative duties of the center. This requirement may be met by having one or more persons on site who meet the requirements for a child care administrator as set forth in G.S. 110-91(8) and according to the licensed capacity of the center.
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention on-site administrator hours.

findings.requirement: Each group of children must have a lead teacher in attendance for at least two-thirds of total daily operating hours.
findings.quote: Each group of children shall have a lead teacher in attendance for at least two-thirds of the total daily hours of operation, based on a normal working schedule, and may include times when the lead teacher may not be in attendance due to circumstances such as illness or vacation.
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention lead teacher attendance for at least two-thirds of daily operating hours.

findings.requirement: Staff may release a child only to an individual listed on the enrollment application.
findings.quote: Center administrators and staff shall release a child only to an individual listed on the application.
findings.handbook_quote: We release children only to parents and to adults listed on the child's authorized pickup form.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that children are released only to authorized individuals.

findings.requirement: Each child must have a completed, signed application for enrollment on file on the first day of attendance.
findings.quote: Each child in care shall have an individual application for enrollment completed and signed by the child's parent, as defined in 10A NCAC 09 .0102. The completed, signed application shall be on file in the center on the first day the child attends
findings.handbook_quote: To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes the enrollment application and required forms.

findings.requirement: Enrollment application information must be accessible to caregiving staff while the child is in care.
findings.quote: The information contained in Subparagraphs (a)(1) through (a)(7) and Paragraph (b) of this Rule, shall be accessible to caregiving staff during the time the child is in care.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child's records are confidential and are shared only with you, our staff and licensing staff.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that enrollment information is accessible to caregiving staff during care.

findings.requirement: Emergency medical care information must be on file for each child and updated as changes occur and at least annually.
findings.quote: This emergency medical care information shall be on file in the center on the child's first day of attendance and shall be updated as changes occur and at least annually.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child's records are confidential and are shared only with you, our staff and licensing staff.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention emergency medical care information on file and updated annually.

findings.requirement: A parent must sign a statement authorizing the center to obtain emergency medical care, on file the first day the child attends.
findings.quote: Each child's parent, legal guardian, or full-time custodian shall sign a statement authorizing the center to obtain medical attention for the child in an emergency. That statement shall be on file on the first day the child attends the center.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child's records are confidential and are shared only with you, our staff and licensing staff.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention a parent-signed authorization for emergency medical care.

findings.requirement: An incident report must be completed each time a child is injured while in care, signed by staff and parent, with a copy to the parent.
findings.quote: This report shall be signed by the person completing it and by the parent, a copy given to the parent or the parent declining a copy and the report maintained in the child's file.
findings.handbook_quote: If your child has a minor injury, we will tell you at pickup and give you a written incident report.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions incident reports but not that staff and parents sign them.
findings.fix: If a child is injured, we complete an incident report, review it with you, and ask you to sign it. We give you a copy and keep the report in your child's file.

findings.requirement: If medical treatment is required from an incident in care, a copy of the incident report must be mailed to the Division within seven calendar days.
findings.quote: When medical treatment is required by a health care professional, community clinic, or local health department as a result of an incident occurring while the child is in care, a copy of the incident report shall be mailed to a representative of the Division within seven calendar days after the incident.
findings.handbook_quote: For a serious injury we will call 911 first and then call you right away.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention mailing an incident report to the Division within seven days when medical treatment is required.

findings.requirement: No medication may be administered without written parental authorization and written instructions, and prescription medication must be stored in original containers with pharmacy labels.
findings.quote: No prescription or over-the-counter medication and no topical, non-medical ointment, repellent, lotion, cream, fluoridated toothpaste, or powder shall be administered to any child: (a) without written authorization from the child's parent; (b) without written instructions from the child's parent, physician or other health professional;
findings.handbook_quote: To make things easier for busy families, you may authorize medication by phone or by text message to your child's teacher, and we will note your permission in the medication log.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows medication authorization by phone or text, while the rule requires written authorization and written instructions.
findings.fix: We give medicine only with your written permission and written instructions. Please complete our medication permission form before any medicine is given; phone or text permission is not enough.

findings.requirement: Each administration of prescription or over-the-counter medication must be recorded with child name, date, time, amount and type, and administrator signature.
findings.quote: Any time prescription or over-the-counter medication is administered by center personnel to children receiving care, the following information shall be recorded: (a) the child's name; (b) the date the medication was given; (c) the time the medication was given; (d) the amount and the type of medication given; and (e) the name and signature of the person administering the medication.
findings.handbook_quote: We can give prescription and over-the-counter medicine during the day when it is necessary. Medicine must be in its original container, labeled with your child's name.
findings.explanation: The handbook says doses are recorded but does not list all required documentation fields.
findings.fix: Each time we give medicine, we record your child's name, the date and time, the amount and type of medicine, and the name and signature of the staff member who gave it.

findings.requirement: Parents must be notified at enrollment if the center provides care for mildly ill children.
findings.quote: notify all parents at enrollment that the center will be providing care for mildly ill children;
findings.handbook_quote: To keep everyone healthy, please keep your child home if they have a fever of 100.4°F or higher, vomiting, diarrhea, an unexplained rash, or are too sick to take part in normal activities.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state whether the center provides care for mildly ill children.

findings.requirement: If medication is administered in error, staff must call 911, notify the director and parent, observe the child, and document the error in the child's file.
findings.quote: If medication is administered in error, whether administering the wrong dosage, giving to the wrong child, or giving the incorrect type of medicine, the child care center shall: (a) call 911 in accordance with CPR or First Aid training recommendations; (b) notify the center director; (c) contact the child's parent; (d) observe the child; and (e) document the medication error in writing
findings.handbook_quote: We can give prescription and over-the-counter medicine during the day when it is necessary. Medicine must be in its original container, labeled with your child's name.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe the procedure for a medication error.

findings.requirement: A child with listed symptoms or conditions, such as fever thresholds, vomiting, diarrhea, lice, scabies, chicken pox, or strep throat, must be excluded from care.
findings.quote: Centers may provide care for a mildly ill infant or child older than two months who has a Fahrenheit temperature less than 101 degrees and for infants younger than two months who have a Fahrenheit temperature of less than 100.4 by any method including axillary or orally, so long as the child does not have any of the following:
findings.handbook_quote: To keep everyone healthy, please keep your child home if they have a fever of 100.4°F or higher, vomiting, diarrhea, an unexplained rash, or are too sick to take part in normal activities.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists some exclusion symptoms but not all conditions required by the rule.
findings.fix: Please keep your child home for the symptoms listed in our illness policy and for other conditions that require exclusion under state rules, such as lice, scabies, chicken pox, strep throat, or a health professional's order.

findings.requirement: A child who becomes ill or is suspected of having a communicable disease must be separated from other children until leaving the center.
findings.quote: separate from the other children any child who becomes ill while in care or who is suspected of having a communicable disease or condition other than as described in Paragraph (a) of this Rule until the child leaves the center;
findings.handbook_quote: If your child becomes ill at the center, we will call you and you must pick up within one hour.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that an ill child is separated from other children until leaving the center.

findings.requirement: If a parent opts out of supplemental food, the parent must sign a statement acknowledging the decision, kept in the child's file and copied to the parent.
findings.quote: A child's parent may opt out of the supplemental food provided by the center as set forth in G.S. 110-91(2)h.1. When a child's parent opts out of the supplemental food provided by the center, the parent shall sign a statement acknowledging the parental decision shall be kept in the child's file at the center and a copy provided to the parent.
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe the parent opt-out process for supplemental food.
findings.fix: If you choose to provide all of your child's meals and snacks, you may opt out of our supplemental food program by signing our opt-out statement. We keep a copy in your child's file and give you a copy.

findings.requirement: Meals and snacks must comply with USDA Meal Patterns for Children in Child Care Programs.
findings.quote: Meals and snacks served to children in a child care center shall comply with the Meal Patterns for Children in Child Care Programs from the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that meals meet USDA nutrition guidelines.

findings.requirement: When food is prepared or provided by the center, a dated copy of the current week's menu must be posted where parents and food staff can see it.
findings.quote: At least one dated copy of the current week's menu shall be posted where it can be seen by parents and food preparation staff when food is prepared or provided by the center.
findings.handbook_quote: The daily menu, including all meals and snacks, is posted at the entrance of each center.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that the daily menu is posted.

findings.requirement: Diapers must be changed whenever soiled or wet, not on a shift basis.
findings.quote: (a) Diapers shall be changed whenever they become soiled or wet and not on a shift basis.
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention diaper changing and toileting hygiene requirements.

findings.requirement: Children's special diets or food allergies must be posted in the food preparation area and the child's eating area.
findings.quote: Children's special diets or food allergies shall be posted where they can be seen in the food preparation area and in the child's eating area.
findings.handbook_quote: Please tell us in writing about any food allergy. For children with a severe allergy, we need an allergy action plan signed by the child's health care provider before the child's first day.
findings.explanation: The handbook addresses allergies but does not state that special diets and allergies are posted in food and eating areas.
findings.fix: We post children's food allergies and special diets in the food preparation area and in the child's eating area.

findings.requirement: The center may serve only specified beverages, including water, milk by age, and 100 percent fruit juice limited to 6 ounces per day.
findings.quote: The child care provider shall serve only the following beverages: (1) breast milk, as specified in Paragraph (k) of this Rule; (2) formula; (3) water; (4) unflavored whole milk, for children ages 12-23 months; (5) unflavored skim or lowfat milk for children 24 months through five years; (6) unflavored skim milk, unflavored low-fat milk, or flavored skim milk for children six years and older; or (7) 100 percent fruit juice, limited to 6 ounces per day, for all ages.
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not list the beverages that may be served.

findings.quote: The parent or health care provider of each child under 15 months of age shall provide the center an individual written feeding plan for the child. This plan shall be followed at the center.
findings.handbook_quote: Infants sleep in individual cribs, following their own schedules.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention individual written feeding plans for infants.

findings.requirement: Meals and snacks must be provided at least every four hours according to the hours a child is in care.
findings.quote: Meals and snacks shall be planned according to the number of hours a child is in the center. Children shall be provided a meal or snack a minimum of every four hours.
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state how often meals and snacks are provided based on hours in care.

findings.requirement: Each adult and child must be restrained with an individual seat belt or child safety seat appropriate to age or weight when transported.
findings.quote: When children enrolled in a child care center are being transported, each adult and child shall be restrained with an individual seat belt or child safety seat appropriate to the child's age or weight in accordance with G.S. 20-135.2A
findings.handbook_quote: For trips by bus, we'll ask you to sign a permission slip.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention seat belts or child safety seats during transportation.

findings.requirement: Vehicles used to transport children must be free of hazards and comply with state and federal laws, and be insured for liability.
findings.quote: Vehicles used to transport children enrolled in child care centers shall be free of hazards such as, but not limited to, torn upholstery that allows children to remove the interior padding, broken windows, holes in the floor or roof, or tire treads of less than 2/32 of an inch.
findings.handbook_quote: For trips by bus, we'll ask you to sign a permission slip.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention vehicle safety or insurance requirements.

findings.requirement: Pick-up and delivery procedures must be communicated to parents and posted where parents can see them.

findings.handbook_quote: Please walk your child into the classroom and sign them in on the tablet at the front desk. A staff member must greet your child before you leave.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that pick-up and delivery procedures are posted where parents can see them.
findings.fix: Our pick-up and delivery procedures are posted where families can see them and are shared with families.

findings.requirement: Written parental permission is required before transporting a child, including when and where, expected times, and provider.
findings.quote: Before children are transported, written permission from a parent shall be obtained that shall include when and where the child is to be transported, expected time of departure and arrival, and the transportation provider.
findings.handbook_quote: For trips by bus, we'll ask you to sign a permission slip.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions permission for bus trips but not all required details for transportation permission.
findings.fix: Before we transport a child, we obtain written permission that includes when and where the child will be transported, expected departure and arrival times, and the transportation provider.

findings.requirement: Parents may give standing permission, valid up to 12 months, for routine transport to and from the center.
findings.quote: Parents may give standing permission, valid for up to 12 months, for transport of children to and from the center not including off premise activities as described in Rule .1005 of this Section.
findings.handbook_quote: For trips by bus, we'll ask you to sign a permission slip.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention standing permission for routine transportation.

findings.requirement: Children must not be left in a vehicle unattended by an adult.
findings.quote: Children shall not be left in a vehicle unattended by an adult.
findings.handbook_quote: For trips by bus, we'll ask you to sign a permission slip.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that children are not left in vehicles unattended.

findings.requirement: A current schedule of off-premise activities must be posted in each participating classroom and a copy given to parents.
findings.quote: The center shall post a schedule of off premise activities in each participating classroom where it can be viewed by parents, and a copy shall be given to parents. The schedule shall be current and shall include the: (A) location of the activity; (B) purpose of the activity; (C) time the activity will take place; (D) date of the activity; and (E) name of the person(s) to be contacted in the event of an emergency.
findings.handbook_quote: Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center. We'll let you know about walking trips on the morning of the trip.
findings.explanation: The handbook notifies families of trips but does not describe a posted schedule with all required details.
findings.fix: We post a current schedule of off-premises activities in each participating classroom and give families a copy. The schedule includes the location, purpose, time, date, and emergency contact.

findings.requirement: Children under three may not participate in off-premise activities involving motor vehicle transport.
findings.quote: Children under the age of three shall not participate in off premise activities that involve children being transported in a motor vehicle.
findings.handbook_quote: Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention restrictions for children under three on off-premises activities involving vehicles.

findings.requirement: Written parental permission is required before walking children off premises for play or outings.
findings.quote: Before staff members walk children off premises for play or outings, the center shall obtain written permission from the parent of each child to be included in such activities.
findings.handbook_quote: Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center. We'll let you know about walking trips on the morning of the trip.
findings.explanation: The handbook notifies families of walking trips but does not state that written permission is obtained.
findings.fix: Before children walk off premises for play or outings, we obtain written permission from each child's parent.

findings.requirement: Parents may give standing permission, valid up to 12 months, for regular off-premise activities.
findings.quote: Parents may provide a written statement giving standing permission which may be valid for up to 12 months for participation in off premise activities that occur on a regular basis.
findings.handbook_quote: Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention standing permission for regular off-premises activities.

findings.requirement: New employees with child contact must receive 16 hours of on-site orientation within the first six weeks, including six hours within the first two weeks.
findings.quote: Each center shall ensure that each new employee who is expected to have contact with children receives 16 hours of on-site orientation within the first six weeks of employment. As part of this orientation, each new employee shall complete six hours of orientation within the first two weeks of employment.
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention the required new staff orientation hours.

findings.requirement: Administrators and staff must complete health and safety training within one year of employment, unless completed within the prior year.
findings.quote: Child care administrators and staff members shall complete health and safety training within one year of employment, unless the staff member has completed the training within the year prior to beginning employment.
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention health and safety training within one year of employment.

findings.requirement: Staff who provide direct care or accompany children off premises must complete First Aid and CPR certification appropriate to the ages of children in care.
findings.quote: All staff who provide direct care or accompany children when they are off premises shall successfully complete certification in First Aid appropriate to the ages of children in care.
findings.handbook_quote: All teachers and the director hold current pediatric first aid certification, and at least one staff member with current pediatric CPR certification is at each center whenever children are present.
findings.explanation: The handbook addresses first aid and CPR but not that all direct care staff complete both certifications.
findings.fix: All staff who provide direct care or accompany children off premises complete pediatric first aid and CPR certification appropriate for the ages of children in care.

findings.requirement: In centers licensed for infants, the administrator and any provider scheduled in the infant room must complete ITS-SIDS training within two months and every three years.
findings.quote: In centers that are licensed to care for infants, the child care administrator and any child care provider scheduled to work in the infant room shall complete ITS-SIDS training. ITS-SIDS training shall be completed within two months of an individual assuming responsibilities in the infant room and every three years thereafter.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention ITS-SIDS training for infant care staff.

findings.requirement: The administrator and all staff must complete Recognizing and Responding to Suspicions of Child Maltreatment training within 90 days of employment.
findings.quote: The child care administrator and all staff members shall complete Recognizing and Responding to Suspicions of Child Maltreatment training within 90 days of employment.
findings.handbook_quote: All lead teachers are at least 18 years old, and every staff member completes a background check before working with children.

findings.requirement: Primary space must provide no more than one child per 25 square feet, and rest periods require at least 200 cubic feet of air space per child.
findings.quote: No room may be occupied by more than one child per 25 square feet of floor space, provided that a room may be occupied by a larger group of children for special activities so long as such occupancy does not violate the State fire code.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are grouped by age. We keep classes small so every child gets attention:
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention indoor space or air space requirements.

findings.requirement: The outdoor play area must be at least 75 square feet per child using it at one time and provide shaded areas.

findings.handbook_quote: Children play outside at least twice a day unless the weather is dangerous.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention outdoor space size or shade requirements.

findings.requirement: Written parental permission is required for aquatic activities and must include awareness of aquatic policies.

findings.handbook_quote: We don't offer swimming or wading pools. Children may play at a water table with a teacher present.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention written permission for aquatic activities.
