findings.requirement: Children with health care needs requiring specialized services must have a medical action plan attached to the application and updated annually.
findings.quote: For any child with health care needs such as allergies, asthma, or other chronic conditions that require specialized health services, a medical action plan shall be attached to the application. The medical action plan shall be updated on an annual basis and when changes to the plan are made by the child's parent or health care professional.
findings.handbook_quote: For children with a severe allergy, we need an allergy action plan signed by the child's health care provider before the child's first day.
findings.explanation: The handbook addresses allergy action plans but not annual updates or attachment to the enrollment application.
findings.fix: For children with health care needs such as allergies or asthma, we keep a medical action plan on file and update it at least once a year or when the plan changes.

findings.requirement: Children must be adequately supervised at all times, with staff positioned to hear or see children and render assistance.
findings.quote: Children shall be adequately supervised at all times in child care centers. Adequate supervision shall mean that: (1) staff must be positioned in the indoor and outdoor environment to maximize their ability to hear or see the children at all times and render assistance;
findings.handbook_quote: A staff member must greet your child before you leave.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe adequate supervision requirements.

findings.requirement: Staff must interact with children in positive ways, including eye contact, conversation, problem-solving support, and positive reinforcement.
findings.quote: Staff shall interact with children in positive ways by helping them feel welcome and comfortable, treating them with respect, listening to what they say, responding to them with acceptance and appreciation, and participating in activities with the children.
findings.handbook_quote: We use positive guidance: clear expectations, redirection, praise and natural consequences.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe required positive staff-child interactions.

findings.requirement: No child may be handled roughly or placed in a locked room, closet, or box or left alone separated from staff.
findings.quote: (1) no child shall be handled roughly in any way, including shaking, pushing, shoving, pinching, slapping, biting, kicking, or spanking; (2) no child shall be placed in a locked room, closet, or box or be left alone in a room separated from staff;
findings.handbook_quote: We never use spanking, shaking or any physical punishment, and we never shame or yell at children.
findings.explanation: The handbook prohibits some discipline practices but not all practices prohibited by the rule.
findings.fix: We never use corporal punishment or rough handling, and we never place a child in a locked room, closet, or box, leave a child alone separated from staff, delegate discipline to another child, withhold food, discipline for toileting accidents or not sleeping, assign hazardous chores, require physical activity as punishment, yell, shame, humiliate, frighten, threaten, bully, or restrain a child except to keep someone safe.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive written notice of discipline policy changes 14 days before implementation, with a signed acknowledgement retained.
findings.quote: If a center changes its discipline policy at any time, it must give written notice of such a change to the child's parent, guardian, or full-time custodian 14 days prior to the implementation of the new policy.
findings.handbook_quote: We use positive guidance: clear expectations, redirection, praise and natural consequences. We never use spanking, shaking or any physical punishment, and we never shame or yell at children.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state that parents receive written notice of discipline policy changes 14 days before implementation.
findings.fix: If we change our discipline policy, we give written notice 14 days before the change takes effect and ask you to sign an acknowledgment.

findings.requirement: Records must be retained for the periods specified, including children's records for as long as enrolled and one year after, and personnel records for at least one year after employment ends.

findings.handbook_quote: We keep attendance and children's records for at least three years after a child leaves our program, or longer if state rules require it.
findings.explanation: The handbook states a records retention period that meets or exceeds the rule.

findings.requirement: Withholding dessert as discipline
findings.quote: no food shall be withheld as punishment or given as a means of reward;

findings.explanation: The handbook withholds dessert as a consequence, while the rule prohibits withholding food as punishment.
findings.fix: We do not withhold food, including dessert, as a consequence. We use positive guidance and work with children and families to address behavior.

NC.summary: The handbook covers many basic policies but omits or conflicts with several North Carolina requirements, including medication authorization, safe sleep for infants, screen time for children under three, and discipline practices. Several required policies and notices are also missing and should be added before the handbook is used for the Durham center.

OR.rulebook: DELC Rules for Certified Child Care Centers, CCLD-0084 (OAR 414-305)

findings.requirement: The handbook must name the person with immediate responsibility for daily operation, with business address and phone number.
findings.quote: Name, business address, and business telephone number of the person(s) who has immediate responsibility for the daily operation of the center;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not name the person with immediate responsibility for daily operation or give a business address and phone number.
findings.fix: Our center's daily operations are led by [Director's name], who can be reached at [business address] and [business phone number]. Please contact them with questions about our program.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe licensed capacity, ages and number of children, hours, days, months, closures, holidays, and ratios.
findings.quote: A center description including the licensed capacity, ages and number of children in care, hours, days and months of operation, closure dates and observed holidays, and staff-to-child ratios;
findings.handbook_quote: Our centers are open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., all year except for the following holidays:
findings.explanation: The handbook covers hours, days, holidays, closures, ages, and ratios but does not state licensed capacity or the number of children in care.
findings.fix: Our certified center is licensed for [number] children. We care for children ages [ages], with [number] children currently enrolled. We are open [days] from [time] to [time], [months], and closed on [holidays/closures]. Our staff-to-child ratios are [ratios].

findings.requirement: The handbook must state arrival and departure procedures, sign-in and sign-out requirements, and authorized pickup persons.
findings.quote: Arrival and departure procedures, including sign in and out requirements and individuals authorized for pick-up;
findings.handbook_quote: Please walk your child into the classroom and sign them in on the tablet at the front desk. A staff member must greet your child before you leave.
findings.explanation: The handbook states arrival sign-in, staff greeting, and authorized pickup procedures.

findings.requirement: The handbook must explain parent responsibilities for providing current required information and what parents must provide.
findings.quote: Parent responsibilities for providing current required information and what parents are expected to provide;
findings.handbook_quote: To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists some enrollment items but does not explain parents' responsibility to keep required information current.
findings.fix: Families are responsible for keeping enrollment, health, immunization, allergy, and emergency contact information current, and for providing items listed in our enrollment forms.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include health policies covering toileting, diapering, handwashing, infant feeding support, bottles and pacifiers, immunization tracking, medication, repellent and sunscreen, bed linen, ill child care, exclusion, and injury response.
findings.quote: Health policies and procedures to include toileting, diaper changing and handwashing methods, support for parents feeding their infants, storage and handling of bottles and pacifiers, immunization tracking, medication administration, use of insect repellent and sunscreen, care of bed linen, care of children who are ill and exclusion criteria, and response to injuries
findings.handbook_quote: Sunscreen and insect repellent. With your written permission, we apply the sunscreen you provide before outdoor play, and insect repellent when needed.
findings.explanation: The handbook addresses some health topics but omits toileting, diapering, handwashing, infant feeding, bottles and pacifiers, immunization tracking, bed linen care, and other required health details.
findings.fix: Our health practices include toileting and diapering, handwashing, supporting families who feed infants, storing bottles and pacifiers, tracking immunizations, giving medication, using sunscreen and insect repellent, caring for bedding, caring for ill children and exclusion criteria, and responding to injuries.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state safety measures including safe sleep, monitoring sleeping infants, injury prevention, pesticides and toxic substances, animals, water activities, and prohibited substances.
findings.quote: Safety measures including safe sleep practices, monitoring of sleeping infants, injury prevention, use of pesticides and other potentially toxic substances, animals, water activities, and prohibited substances;
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are placed on their backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib.
findings.explanation: The handbook covers safe sleep and some safety topics but does not address pesticides, toxic substances, or prohibited substances.
findings.fix: Our safety practices include safe sleep and monitoring sleeping infants, preventing injuries, storing pesticides and toxic substances out of reach, supervising animals and water play, and keeping prohibited substances off the premises.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include a plan ensuring visitors or other adults not enrolled or conditionally enrolled in the CBR do not have unsupervised access to children.
findings.quote: A plan to ensure that any visitor or other adult not enrolled or conditionally enrolled in the CBR does not have unsupervised access to children;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not include a plan to prevent visitors or other adults not enrolled in the Central Background Registry from having unsupervised access to children.
findings.fix: Visitors and other adults who are not enrolled in Oregon's Central Background Registry are never left alone with children. A staff member signs them in and out and stays with them while they are in the center.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include the emergency preparedness plan.
findings.quote: Emergency preparedness plan (also see OAR 414-305-0210, Emergency Preparedness and Response);
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions drills but does not describe the full written emergency preparedness plan.
findings.fix: Our written emergency plan covers evacuation, relocation, shelter-in-place, lockdown, medical emergencies, and reunification. We review it with staff each year and practice drills regularly.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the center philosophy on how children learn and develop and how it is implemented.
findings.quote: Center philosophy on how children learn and develop, and how this philosophy is implemented;
findings.handbook_quote: We believe children learn best through play, relationships and a safe, predictable day.
findings.explanation: The handbook states the center's philosophy and how it is carried out in daily care.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include daily schedules with planned activities, rest time, physical activity, and screen time.
findings.quote: Daily schedules that include planned activities, rest time, physical activity, and screen time;
findings.handbook_quote: Each day includes indoor and outdoor play, circle time, small-group activities, meals and rest.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes daily activities, rest, physical activity, and screen time.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe center-sponsored religious and cultural activities and how holidays are recognized.
findings.quote: Center-sponsored religious and cultural activities, if any, including how holidays will be recognized;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe center-sponsored religious or cultural activities or how holidays are recognized.
findings.fix: We do not sponsor religious activities. We recognize holidays by [description], and families may choose whether their child participates.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state meals, snacks, and food service practices including storage and handling, dietary needs and allergies, infant feeding, and food from home.
findings.quote: Meals, snacks, and food service practices including food storage and handling, children’s dietary needs and allergies, infant feeding, and food brought from the child’s home;
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions meals and allergies but does not address food storage and handling, infant feeding, or food brought from home.
findings.fix: We store and handle food safely, accommodate dietary needs and allergies, support infant feeding, and follow our policy for food brought from home.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state transportation and field trip policies including driver and vehicle requirements and supervision.
findings.quote: Transportation and field trips including driver and vehicle requirements and supervision;
findings.handbook_quote: Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center. We'll let you know about walking trips on the morning of the trip.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions walking trips and bus permission slips but does not state driver and vehicle requirements or supervision practices.
findings.fix: For field trips and transportation, we follow driver and vehicle requirements, maintain supervision, and obtain written parent permission with dates, times, and locations.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include the behavior and guidance policy.
findings.quote: (m) Transportation and field trips including driver and vehicle requirements and supervision; (n) Behavior and guidance policies;
findings.handbook_quote: We use positive guidance: clear expectations, redirection, praise and natural consequences.
findings.explanation: The handbook includes a behavior and guidance policy.

findings.requirement: The handbook must explain how staff proceed if a child displays inappropriate behaviors that could endanger themselves or others.
findings.quote: How staff must proceed if a child is displaying inappropriate behaviors that could endanger themselves or the safety of others;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not explain how staff proceed when a child displays behaviors that could endanger themselves or others.
findings.fix: If a child's behavior could endanger themselves or others, staff will stay close, help the child regain control, and follow our behavior and guidance policy. We will contact the family and work together on supports.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe communication methods, notifications, and how parent grievances, questions, or concerns are handled.
findings.quote: Communication methods and notifications, including how parent grievances, questions, or concerns are handled by the center;
findings.handbook_quote: We share updates through our parent app and hold parent-teacher conferences twice a year.
findings.explanation: The handbook describes communication methods, notifications, and how concerns are handled.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state prevention of and duty to report suspected child abuse and neglect.
findings.quote: Any staff member who has reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected is required to report the matter immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline
findings.handbook_quote: If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director, who looks into the concern and decides whether to contact child protective services.
findings.explanation: The handbook routes suspected abuse through the director and makes reporting discretionary, while the rule requires any staff member to report immediately.
findings.fix: Any staff member who suspects child abuse or neglect reports it immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline, DHS Child Welfare, or law enforcement.

findings.requirement: The handbook must describe evening and night care if provided.
findings.quote: Evening and night care, if provided;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe night care, and the center's stated hours do not include night care.

findings.requirement: The handbook must explain how to view inspection reports, access DELC website and center certification rules, and contact CCLD and the child abuse and neglect hotline.
findings.quote: How to view inspection reports, access the Department of Early Learning and Care website and center certification rules, and contact CCLD and child abuse and neglect hotline;
findings.handbook_quote: You have the right to visit your child at any time we are open, to see your child's records, to see our most recent licensing inspection report (posted at the entrance), and to contact the state licensing agency with any concern about our program.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions inspection reports and contacting licensing but does not explain how to access the DELC website, center certification rules, or the child abuse and neglect hotline.
findings.fix: Families can view our most recent inspection report, access the Department of Early Learning and Care website and our certification rules, and find CCLD and child abuse and neglect hotline contact information at [location].

findings.requirement: The handbook must advise parents that they can access information about child care providers on the child care safety portal.
findings.quote: A statement advising parents that they can access information about child care providers on the child care safety portal.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not advise parents that they can access information about child care providers on the child care safety portal.
findings.fix: Families can find information about child care providers, including our center, on Oregon's child care safety portal.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include the suspension and expulsion prevention policy.
findings.quote: Suspension and expulsion prevention policy (OAR 414-305-0750).
findings.explanation: The handbook does not include a suspension and expulsion prevention policy.
findings.fix: We work to keep children in care. If a young child is facing possible expulsion, we document concerns, try supports, contact Every Child Belongs, and partner with the family.

findings.requirement: The center must complete an individualized assessment when aware a child with specific needs has applied or is in care, documenting needed modifications.
findings.quote: a certified child care center must complete an individualized assessment whenever the center becomes aware that a child with specific needs has either applied for enrollment or is already in care at the center.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention the individualized assessment process for children with specific needs.

findings.requirement: The center must practice evacuation drills monthly and one other emergency plan aspect every other month.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must practice evacuation drills monthly and one other aspect of the emergency plan every other month that:
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and calmly. We also practice shelter-in-place and lockdown drills several times a year.
findings.explanation: The handbook states monthly fire drills but does not state that one other emergency plan aspect is practiced every other month.
findings.fix: We practice evacuation drills every month and practice one other part of our emergency plan every other month.

findings.requirement: The center must comply with Oregon Health Authority immunization rules for children.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must comply with Oregon Health Authority’s administrative rules (see OAR 333-050-0040) relating to the immunization of children.
findings.handbook_quote: To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires an immunization record at enrollment.

findings.requirement: Parent permission for a field trip must be specific with dates, times, and locations for each field trip.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must have parent permission prior to a field trip or other activity away from the immediate neighborhood. Field trip permission must be specific with dates, times, and locations for each field trip.
findings.handbook_quote: Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center. We'll let you know about walking trips on the morning of the trip.
findings.explanation: The handbook gives notice of walking trips but does not obtain written parent permission with dates, times, and locations before each trip.
findings.fix: We obtain written parent permission before any field trip or activity away from the immediate neighborhood. Permission lists the date, time, and location of each trip.

findings.requirement: A child may only be released to a parent or another person named and identified by the parent, with identification if not known to staff.
findings.quote: A certified child care center may only release a child to a parent or another person named and identified by the parent(s). A person picking up the child must show identification if not known to staff.
findings.handbook_quote: We release children only to parents and to adults listed on the child's authorized pickup form.
findings.explanation: The handbook limits release to parents and authorized adults and requires identification when needed.

findings.requirement: Child and personnel records must be kept confidential and available only to necessary personnel, the child's parents, and CCLD staff.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must keep child and personnel records confidential and only available to personnel as necessary, the individual child's parents, and CCLD staff.
findings.handbook_quote: Your child's records are confidential and are shared only with you, our staff and licensing staff.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that child records are confidential and shared only with appropriate parties.

findings.requirement: Custodial parents have access to all child care areas upon notifying any staff member during hours of operation and without advance notice.
findings.quote: A notice that custodial parents have access to all child care areas upon notifying any staff member of their presence during the hours of operation and without advance notice;
findings.handbook_quote: Parents are welcome to visit at any time during our hours, without calling first.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows parents to visit during operating hours without advance notice.

findings.requirement: The center must post information on how to report a complaint to CCLD regarding certification requirements.
findings.quote: Information on how to report a complaint to CCLD regarding certification requirements;
findings.handbook_quote: You may also contact your state's child care licensing office at any time. The office's phone number is posted at the entrance.
findings.explanation: The handbook tells families how to contact the licensing office and where that information is posted.

findings.requirement: Any staff member who suspects child abuse or neglect must report immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline, DHS Child Welfare, or law enforcement.
findings.quote: Any staff member who has reason to believe a child has been abused or neglected is required to report the matter immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline
findings.handbook_quote: If a staff member suspects that a child has been abused or neglected, they tell the center director, who looks into the concern and decides whether to contact child protective services.
findings.explanation: The handbook makes reporting discretionary and routed through the director, while the rule requires immediate reporting by any staff member.
findings.fix: Any staff member who suspects child abuse or neglect reports it immediately to the Oregon Child Abuse Hotline, DHS Child Welfare, or law enforcement.

findings.requirement: Centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001 must use Table 3A ratios and group sizes, such as 1:4 for infants and 1:15 for school-age children.
findings.quote: 6 weeks to 24 months of age 1:4 8
findings.handbook_quote: Sprouts 1 – 2 years 1 to 6 12
findings.explanation: The handbook lists ratios and group sizes that exceed Oregon's required Table 3A ratios for infants, toddlers, preschool-age, and school-age children.
findings.fix: We follow Oregon's required staff-to-child ratios and group sizes for our center's certification, including 1:4 for infants, 1:5 for toddlers 24-36 months, 1:10 for preschool-age children, and 1:15 for school-age children.

findings.requirement: Staff must supervise children within sight and sound without relying on audio or video monitoring devices, except as specified.
findings.quote: Be within sight and sound, without relying on audio or video monitoring devices, except as specified in OAR 414-305-0500(4).
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe supervision methods such as sight and sound requirements.

findings.requirement: The center must not provide care for a child under six weeks of age.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must not provide care for a child under six weeks of age.
findings.handbook_quote: We are a nonprofit early learning program serving children from 6 weeks through 5 years old, with after-school care for children up to age 12 at our Austin location.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that care begins at 6 weeks of age.

findings.requirement: Infants must be placed on their backs on a flat, firm, non-inclined surface for sleeping.
findings.quote: If an infant arrives asleep in a car seat or falls asleep in a place other than their crib, portable crib or play yard, the caregiver must immediately move the infant to an appropriate sleep surface.
findings.handbook_quote: To avoid waking a baby, infants who fall asleep in a bouncer, swing or car seat may finish their nap there as long as a teacher can see them.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows infants to finish naps in bouncers, swings, or car seats, while the rule requires moving them immediately to an appropriate sleep surface.
findings.fix: Infants are placed on their backs on a flat, firm sleep surface. If an infant falls asleep in a bouncer, swing, or car seat, we move them to their crib right away.

findings.requirement: The center must not use or threaten prohibited discipline, including corporal punishment, isolation, food withdrawal, or humiliation.
findings.quote: Withdrawing, denying or forcing food, rest, or toileting;
findings.handbook_quote: Children who throw food or refuse to sit at lunch may lose their dessert for that day.
findings.explanation: The handbook denies dessert as a consequence, while the rule prohibits withdrawing or denying food.
findings.fix: We never withdraw or deny food as a consequence. We use positive guidance and, when needed, a brief supervised break to help a child regain control.

findings.requirement: Physical restraint may only be used when a child's safety or others' safety is threatened, gently and for the minimum time necessary.
findings.quote: Physical restraint must only be used if a child's safety or the safety of others is threatened and must be: (a) Limited to holding a child as gently as possible to accomplish restraint;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention physical restraint.

findings.requirement: The center must not exceed licensed capacity at any time, including children in care away from the center.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must not exceed its licensed capacity at any time, including the total number of children in care both at and away from the center.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention licensed capacity limits.

findings.requirement: The center must provide at least 35 square feet of activity space per child.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must have a minimum of 35 square feet of activity space per child.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention activity space requirements.

findings.requirement: The center must provide at least 75 square feet of outdoor activity space per child using the space at one time.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must provide an outdoor activity space of no less than 75 square feet for each child using the space at one time
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention outdoor space requirements.

findings.requirement: The center must not accept a child diagnosed as having or being a carrier of a child care restrictable disease without written approval.
findings.quote: (a) Is diagnosed as having or being a carrier of a child care restrictable disease, as defined in Oregon Health Authority administrative rules, except with the written approval
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention restrictable disease exclusion requirements.

findings.requirement: Any injury that may need physician evaluation or impact to a child's head must be reported to parents immediately and documented.
findings.quote: Any injury that may need evaluation by a physician or impact to a child’s head must be reported to the child’s parent(s) immediately and documented.
findings.handbook_quote: If your child has a minor injury, we will tell you at pickup and give you a written incident report.
findings.explanation: The handbook delays reporting minor injuries until pickup, while the rule requires immediate reporting of head impacts and injuries needing physician evaluation.
findings.fix: We notify parents right away about any injury that may need a doctor's care or any bump or hit to a child's head, and we document it.

findings.requirement: Before giving medication, the center must have signed, dated, written parent authorization on file.
findings.quote: Have a signed, dated, written authorization by the parent(s) on file
findings.handbook_quote: To make things easier for busy families, you may authorize medication by phone or by text message to your child's teacher, and we will note your permission in the medication log.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows general phone or text medication authorization, while the rule requires signed written authorization on file, with phone permission only for a single dose of nonprescription medication.
findings.fix: We need a signed, dated written parent authorization before giving medication. Phone permission is used only for a single dose of nonprescription medication and is documented and signed by the parent at pickup.

findings.requirement: Children in care more than 3.5 consecutive hours must be served a meal or snack every 3.5 hours.
findings.quote: Children in care for more than 3 ½ consecutive hours must be served a meal or snack every 3 ½ hours;
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines.
findings.explanation: The handbook lists meals served but does not state that children in care more than 3.5 hours receive a meal or snack every 3.5 hours.
findings.fix: Children in care more than 3 1/2 hours are offered a meal or snack at least every 3 1/2 hours.

findings.requirement: Children must never be left unattended inside or outside of a vehicle.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must never leave children unattended inside or outside of a vehicle.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not mention transportation supervision requirements.

findings.requirement: Written parent permission is required before engaging in any swimming activities.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must have written permission from each child’s parent before engaging in any swimming activities.
findings.explanation: The handbook states that swimming and wading pools are not offered.

findings.requirement: Parents must be informed of any animals on the premises by a clearly viewed notice, policy handbook, parent flier, or enrollment statement.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must inform parents of any animals on the premises by a clearly viewed notice or bulletin, policy handbook, parent flier, or a statement included on the enrollment form
findings.handbook_quote: We don't keep classroom pets; if a visitor brings an animal, we tell families in advance.
findings.explanation: The handbook informs families about animals brought to the center.

findings.requirement: A center must be approved by CCLD before providing night care.
findings.quote: A certified child care center must be approved by CCLD to provide night care, as defined in 414-305-0100(32).
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe night care.

OR.summary: The handbook covers many family-facing policies but has several gaps and conflicts with Oregon certified child care center rules, especially around abuse reporting, ratios, safe sleep, discipline, injuries, and medication authorization. Updating the listed items will bring the handbook into closer alignment with the rulebook.
